answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may claim rewards, with payouts delayed until peers validate its work. A kernel of randomly selected reviewers checks claims against evidence; proven fraud burns the stake and blocks withdrawal. This makes a meadow of fake accounts costly: an attacker must fund every identity and risk losing each bond, while splitting one stake among many accounts does not multiply voting weight. The zenith of the defense is economic friction, not proof that identities are unique.
